summary_responses.response: The National Credit Union Administration (NCUA) Board has issued a final rule, effective January 4, 2027, amending its criteria for determining associational common bonds for single associational and multiple common bond federal credit unions. The rule clarifies that requiring members to purchase a good, product, or service as a condition of membership will no longer automatically disqualify a group as a recognized association, although groups based primarily on a client-customer relationship remain ineligible. Instead, NCUA will evaluate the totality of the circumstances, and the final rule—revised after public comment—details how the agency assesses client-customer relationships and provides relevant examples. The rule also simplifies NCUA's process for reviewing pre-approved groups, aiming to increase transparency and efficiency. summary_responses.response: The FAA is proposing a new airworthiness directive for certain Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH Model EC135P1, EC135P2, EC135P2+, EC135P3, EC135T1, EC135T2, EC135T2+, EC135T3, and EC635T2+ helicopters with serial numbers up to and including 1276. summary_responses.subtopic: National Park Administration, Conservation & Multi-Use Trail Regulation
summary_responses.response: The National Park Service has issued a final rule, effective December 21, 2026, amending Mammoth Cave National Park's special regulations to expand bicycle and horseback riding opportunities. The rule authorizes the superintendent to designate approximately 37 miles of multi-use trails for bicycles—including eight new trails to be constructed—while removing bicycle access from the White Oak Trail and the Maple Springs Connector Trail that will be closed. It also permits horseback riding on the 5.4-mile Houchin Ferry North/Ollie Road, creating shorter loop options and river access for equestrians despite a general prohibition on horses on park roads. The changes implement part of the park's Comprehensive Land and River Trails Plan and Environmental Assessment, whose preferred alternative was selected in a December 2024 Finding of No Significant Impact after public comment. The plan aims to improve the deteriorated trail system's sustainability and visitor experience using erosion-control and mitigation measures, while the superintendent will notify the public of designated trails—and any e-bike allowances—through the compendium, maps, and park website.
